scgsim-kind: "course"

After you prepare a run, you can look at exactly what the solver will receive:
the mesh, the material of each region, and the boundaries. Do this when a
result looks wrong, or before a long run. It needs the `visualization` extra
(see [Install SCGSim](installation.qmd)).

This step is optional. It does not solve anything.

## Palace: view the mesh and assignments

After `sim.mesh()` and `sim.write_config()`, open the run directory:

```python
from scgsim.visualization import inspect_palace_geometry

preview = inspect_palace_geometry(sim.output_dir)
preview.show_materials()
preview.show_boundaries()
preview.show_surface_epr()
preview.show_mesh()
```

Each view colours regions by the exact Entity and material names in the mesh
file, with a legend. Check them against the Nets and materials you intended.
For an interactive 3D view with rotation and zoom, use
`preview.explore("materials")`.

Run these before `prepare_handoff()` if you want the images included in the
run directory you send to the solver host.

### Mesh summary

```python
summary = sim.mesh_summary()
summary["meshing"]["requested"]   # the mesh settings you asked for
summary["meshing"]["effective"]   # the settings Gmsh actually used
```

The summary reports element and node counts per region, the geometry and
element order, and edge-length statistics in micrometres. Two things to know:

- Edge lengths are straight-line distances between element corners, not
  lengths along curved edges.
- For Eigenmode, the summary includes an *estimated* number of unknowns. Palace
  reports the actual number after the run; the two can differ.

### Mesh quality

```python
quality = sim.check_mesh_quality()
print(quality.show_summary())
print(quality.show_worst_elements(metric="kappa_j", limit=10))
quality.show_elements(metric="volume", limit=10).show()
```

This ranks the tetrahedra by shape metrics so you can find badly shaped
elements. It does not set a pass/fail threshold or fix the mesh. See
[Mesh quality](../mesh-quality.qmd) for the metrics and their units.

## AEDT: build the model without solving

`prepare_handoff()` for AEDT writes files without opening AEDT, so there is
no native model to look at yet. To build the model in AEDT and inspect it
without solving, run this on the AEDT computer from the run directory:

```bash
python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --execute --prepare-only
```

AEDT builds and checks the model, saves the project and closes. No solve
runs.

::: {.callout-important}
A run directory used with `--prepare-only` cannot be solved afterwards.
Prepare a new run directory for the actual solve.
:::

Then open the saved project:

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import parse_aedt_spec
from scgsim.visualization import inspect_aedt_geometry

run_dir = Path(".")  # the prepare-only run directory
spec = parse_aedt_spec(json.loads((run_dir / "aedt_spec.json").read_text()))
receipt = json.loads((run_dir / "metadata/aedt_run_receipt.json").read_text())
project_path = run_dir / receipt["project"]

preview = inspect_aedt_geometry(project_path, design=spec.design_name)
preview.show_materials()
preview.show_boundaries()
```

This opens AEDT to read the project, so it needs AEDT and a licence. Some
views, such as surface EPR and mesh, may not be available for AEDT projects.
See [Geometry preview](../geometry-preview.qmd) for all options.
